class.name: BulletSpawner2D
class.brief_description: Fires timed volleys of bullets through a [BulletFactory2D].
class.description: Assign a [BulletFactory2D], a [BulletVolleyData2D], and a [member pattern_source]. Each volley collects one global transform per bullet from the [member transforms_generator] (empty means this node; a generator outside the tree while the spawner is inside also falls back to this node) and spawns it through the factory. It never fires in the editor. Homing quick-start: turn on [member homing_enabled], leave [member homing_target_source] on Node Group, and put your targets (any Node2D) in a group and name it in [member homing_node_group] (there is no default group: you decide who is chased). Every volley then chases [member homing_target_selection] targets with [member homing_smoothing] turn rate. Set [member homing_target_source] to Mouse to chase the cursor instead, and turn on [member orbiting_enabled] to make bullets ring their target once they arrive. Use [member homing_retarget_mode] so flying volleys keep following fresh targets, and [signal volley_bullet_homing_target_reached] to react when a bullet arrives. Pattern quick-start: pick a [member pattern_source] helper (Ring, Fan, Spiral, Rose, Corridor...) or call [method apply_pattern_preset] for a starter, tune the matching helper_* group, and call [method shoot_once] (or enable [member shooting_enabled] for the auto loop). Add [member pattern_scale] / spin for motion, [member helper_skip_indices] for dodge doors, and [method spawn_pattern_list] for phased sequences. See [member pattern_source] for the full 33-mode list. [b]Steering features and how they mix[/b] (each group has a master switch; every switch works on its own with sane defaults): - [b]Homing[/b] ([member homing_enabled]): bullets turn toward a target at [member homing_smoothing] radians per second. Needs a target source (a group, path, name, the mouse...). Turns first every tick. - [b]Orbiting[/b] ([member orbiting_enabled]): bullets that reach their homing target circle it. Depends on homing; a locked orbit owns the bullet (the flock never turns it). - [b]Flocking[/b] ([member flock_enabled]): bullets avoid each other, line up and group. Works alone (an empty [member flock] flies the default rules); with homing it bends the homing heading, so a homing swarm spreads out on its way and buzzes around its target. Its separation (10 rad/s by default) outpaces the default homing (5 rad/s): raise [member homing_smoothing] above it for bullets that bunch up and hit fast. - [b]Graze[/b] ([member graze_enabled]): reports bullets passing near targets ([signal bullet_grazed]); changes no motion, mixes with everything. - [b]Randomization[/b] ([member bullet_scale_mode] and friends): random sizes, rotations and speeds per bullet. The flock, graze rings ([member GrazeZone2D.count_bullet_size]) and homing reach ([member homing_reach_counts_bullet_size]) count each bullet's own size. - Spawn-data features (wobble, rotation data, direction curves, bounce, gravity) run after homing and the flock: wobble sways on top, rotation data that spins a sprite owns its rotation, a bounce reflects the heading. Call [method debug_explain_features] to read, in plain sentences, what each group will do with the current settings and why one would do nothing. [b]Recipes:[/b] - [i]Homing swarm chasing the player:[/i] [code]homing_enabled = true[/code], [code]homing_node_group = &"player"[/code], [code]flock_enabled = true[/code]. Bullets spread out while they close in. - [i]Burst that fans out, then flocks:[/i] [code]burst_enabled = true[/code], a Ring or Fan pattern, [code]flock_enabled = true[/code] with [member flock_scope] Shared: each shot opens up for [member BulletFlock2D.blend_in_sec], then the shots merge into one swarm. - [i]Random-size swarm that never overlaps:[/i] [code]bullet_scale_mode = Uniform[/code] (0.5 to 2), [code]flock_enabled = true[/code], [code]flock = BulletFlock2D.create_preset(BulletFlock2D.PRESET_KEEP_DISTANCE)[/code]. - [i]Graze-able swarm:[/i] the homing swarm above plus [code]graze_enabled = true[/code], one [GrazeZone2D] in [member graze_zones] and [member graze_node_group] naming the player: score points while dodging. - [i]Orbit ring that keeps its spacing:[/i] [code]homing_enabled = true[/code], [code]orbiting_enabled = true[/code], [code]flock_enabled = true[/code] with the Keep Distance preset: bullets space out while they fly in, then lock into the ring. Reparenting is safe: removing the spawner from the tree and adding it back keeps assigned nodes, tracked homing volleys, burst chains, telegraphs and pattern lists. They pause while the spawner is out of the tree and resume when it returns. Node paths are rewritten from the live nodes on re-entry, so saving the scene keeps the right targets.

method.name: adopt_live_volley
method.description: Takes ownership of a manually-woken volley (manual wake detaches the previous owner): stamps it, replaces the previous spawner's reached forwarder with its own, and tracks it for retargeting. Homing queues are left alone; splits and emitter shots the volley queued and the factory has not spawned yet become this spawner's. Handlers you connected directly on the volley are kept; only spawner forwarders are replaced. Returns false for null or non-live instances.

method.name: aim_live_volleys_at
method.description: Every bullet this spawner fired turns to fly toward [param position] (a direction curve keeps steering its bullets, with one warning). Returns how many volleys changed.

method.name: apply_to_live_volleys
method.description: Applies the chosen groups ([constant PatternSpawner2D.LIVE_ALL] by default) as they stand now to every volley this spawner owns (live or parked): change a setting mid-fight, then call this and the bullets already flying follow. Graze and sound arm the volleys not armed with the current settings and disarm them while their group is off; flocking and splitting arm the volleys fired while off (turning them off already reaches flying bullets); homing arms the volleys fired without it (targets resolved now, with [signal homing_targets_resolved] and [signal volley_homing_configured]; a parked volley, whose frozen bullets take no targets, is armed the same way when it wakes) and clears every chase while off, parked volleys included (a cleared volley leaves the retarget list, so turning homing on again arms it again); a volley that [method BulletVolley2D.homing_follow]s a [BulletTargets2D] keeps its own targets, also when it wakes. A volley already armed alike is left alone, so spent graze rings stay spent. Returns how many volleys changed.

method.name: clear_active_bullets
method.description: Clears every live bullet this spawner owns and returns how many were cleared. With [param fire_clear_effects] (default) the On Clear effect layers fire at each bullet's pose; [code]false[/code] removes them silently. Emptied volleys return to the pool. Other spawners' bullets are untouched.

method.name: clear_live_volleys_homing
method.description: Kill-switch: clears homing queues and stops orbiting on every tracked volley (live or parked: a wake never resumes the chase), through engine clears that keep all counters exact. Returns how many volleys were touched. Retargeting re-arms them while homing stays on; turn homing off (or clear tracking) to keep them flying straight. It also ends a volley's [method BulletVolley2D.homing_follow], so nothing refills the queues.

method.name: collect_shot_colors
method.description: Returns the colors the next shot of [param count] bullets would wear, without firing (empty while [member bullet_color_mode] is Off). With a [member bullet_random_seed] the Random mode returns exactly the next shot's colors; unseeded it draws fresh numbers.

method.name: convert_live_bullets_to_pickups
method.description: Turns every live bullet of the volleys this spawner fired into pickups described by [param pickup]: the way to say "when the boss dies, all its bullets become gems and fly to the player". Other spawners' bullets are left alone (use [method BulletFactory2D.convert_all_bullets_to_pickups] for everything). Returns the new pickup volleys. Needs a factory; the bullets stop counting against [member max_live_bullets]. The converted bullets leave their volleys (silently, or with their On Clear effects when [member BulletPickupData2D.fire_clear_effects] is on) and reappear as pickups at the same pose, scaled by [member BulletPickupData2D.scale_multiplier]. Pickups are owned by the factory, follow [member BulletFactory2D.time_scale] and are never converted again. Collecting one emits [signal BulletFactory2D.pickup_collected]. [param target] is where the pickups are pulled: a [Node2D] (followed while it moves), a [Vector2] (a global position), a group name as a String or StringName (each pickup goes to the nearest usable member of that group at the moment of the call), or null (the mouse cursor). Anything else, an empty group, or a node outside the tree pushes one error and converts nothing.

method.name: debug_explain_features
method.description: Explains the spawner's steering features in plain sentences, one per group: Homing (its source, how many targets it finds right now, its turn rate and reach), Orbiting, Flocking (which flock and preset, the scope, the turn cap and blend-in, how it mixes with homing and orbiting), Graze (zones, source, targets found now, whether rings count bullet size) and Randomization (when sizes vary), followed by the setup warnings. A readout that changes nothing: the seeded random and round-robin homing picks of the next shots stay the same. Use it when a feature seems to do nothing: [codeblock] for line in $BulletSpawner2D.debug_explain_features(): print(line) # Homing: on, source Node Group, 0 target(s) found now. Bullets fly straight until a target appears ... [/codeblock]

method.name: debug_get_retarget_countdown
method.description: Seconds until the next interval retarget pass. Deterministically staggered per spawner so N spawners never group-scan on the same tick.

method.name: forget_tracked_volleys
method.description: Empties the retarget list (the volleys [method retarget_live_volleys] steers). The volleys themselves keep flying and keep reporting to this spawner.

method.name: get_active_live_bullet_count
method.description: Total live bullets across ALL volleys owned by this spawner (counted via the factory by ownership - plain non-homing volleys count exactly like tracked homing volleys). Budget governors and wave gates read this alongside max_live_bullets.

method.name: get_effective_emitter
method.description: Returns the timing in use: [member emitter], or a default [BulletEmitterData2D] (every 0.5 s, along the flight heading) while it is empty.

method.name: get_emitter_template
method.description: Returns the template spawner [member emitter_spawner_path] names now, or [code]null[/code] when it is empty, missing or not a [PatternSpawner2D].

method.name: get_live_volley_count
method.description: How many live volleys this spawner owns (factory census).

method.name: get_live_volleys
method.description: Every live volley this spawner owns (a census of the factory, not capped by the retarget list), so scripts can call the full [BulletVolley2D] API on each. Handles can go stale: a volley whose last bullet died returns to the pool and may serve another owner, so compare [method BulletVolley2D.get_life_id] or check [method BulletVolley2D.is_pooled] before steering a volley you held across frames.

method.name: get_tracked_volley_count
method.description: How many volleys are on the retarget list (every live or parked homing volley this spawner fired or adopted; no cap). A parked volley stays on it and is retargeted again once woken.

method.name: home_live_volleys_to
method.description: Every bullet this spawner fired chases [param target] now: a [Node2D], a [Vector2], a group name (each bullet the nearest member, filtered like every homing target) or [code]null[/code] (the mouse), with the Homing group's steering even when they were fired without homing. A retarget pass of the Homing group may replace it later (set [member homing_retarget_mode] to Off to keep it). Anything else errors and changes nothing. Returns how many volleys changed. An explicit order: it ends a volley's [method BulletVolley2D.homing_follow] (the implicit re-applies leave a following volley alone).

method.name: override_live_volleys_velocity
method.description: Sets the exact velocity of every bullet this spawner fired (live or parked, homing or not). A speed curve overrides direct velocity: the engine warns and keeps the curve's for those bullets. Must be finite. Returns how many volleys changed.

method.name: resolve_homing_targets
method.description: Resolves the current homing targets without touching any volley: group members, name matches (case-insensitive unless [member homing_node_name_case_sensitive]), children of the parent path, the node at [member homing_target_path], or the [member homing_global_position] snapshot. The Mouse source returns an empty array (the cursor is pushed live, not resolved). Entries are Node2D or Vector2. Unless quiet is true, an empty result warns once per homing configuration (shots share the same warning). With advance_round_robin off, the round-robin pick is resolved without consuming the cursor (retarget passes use this so flying volleys keep stable targets).

method.name: retarget_live_volleys
method.description: Homing's refresh (the counterpart of [method refresh_graze_targets]): call it after spawning enemies so flying volleys chase them too, whatever [member homing_retarget_mode] says. Re-resolves targets and replaces the queues of every still-active volley owned by this spawner (expired or pooled volleys are skipped), and re-applies steering and orbiting tuning so runtime changes reach flying volleys. Random and round-robin selections resolve per volley. Volleys with no resolvable targets are skipped quietly and keep their old queues. Volleys whose bullets are all disabled are skipped too: the tick never moves disabled slots, so pushing targets there would only inflate counters. Returns how many volleys were retargeted. Also runs automatically when [member homing_retarget_mode] is On Interval. Only the newest volley is touched when [member homing_retarget_previous_volleys] is off. Locked orbit rings survive the replace per the lock policy ([member orbiting_lock_policy]) instead of always re-locking.

method.name: sample_bullet_color
method.description: Returns the color at [param t] (clamped to 0..1) of [member bullet_color_gradient], or of the built-in red-to-magenta rainbow while it is empty.

method.name: scale_live_volleys_speed
method.description: Speed, top speed and acceleration of every bullet this spawner fired times [param factor] ([code]0[/code] stops them; must be finite and [code]>= 0[/code]). Speed curves keep theirs. Returns how many volleys changed.

method.name: set_live_volleys_speed
method.description: Every bullet this spawner fired flies at [param speed] along its direction (see [method BulletVolley2D.set_bullet_speed]: a capped [member BulletSpeedData2D.max_speed] rises, speed curves keep theirs with a warning). Returns how many volleys changed.

members.member: Gradient Per Shot: how many shots one trip along the gradient takes. Shot [code]k[/code] samples [code](k % cycle) / (cycle - 1)[/code], so the first shot wears the gradient's start and shot [code]cycle - 1[/code] its end. Must be at least 1 (1 holds the start).
The colors the bullets are picked from. Empty uses a built-in rainbow from red to magenta. Edits apply from the next shot.

Gives every fired bullet its own color (see [enum BulletColorMode]). The colors are handed to the factory with the shot, so [member spawn_data] is never changed; a mode beats the data's own [member BulletVolleyData2D.bullet_colors], and Off fires the data's colors (or none). Colored volleys pool separately: pre-warm them with [code]populate_bullets_pool(VolleyPoolKey2D.make(n, shape, true), data, count)[/code]. Split children wear their parent bullet's color. Change a bullet's color later with [method BulletVolley2D.set_bullet_color].

Gradient Across Pattern: how far along the gradient the colors move each shot. 0 keeps every shot alike (bullet [code]i[/code] of [code]n[/code] samples [code]i / (n - 1)[/code]); any other value wraps the gradient around (bullet [code]i[/code] samples [code]i / n + shots * shift[/code]), so a ring's rainbow turns from shot to shot. Must be finite.
Path to the [BulletFactory2D] used for spawning. Inside the tree, a path to a node of another type is rejected (old value kept).
Upper end of the per-bullet lifetime multiplier (see [member bullet_life_time_scale_min]). Finite and > 0.

Lower end of the per-bullet lifetime multiplier: every bullet of a shot lives its lifetime (its own [member BulletVolleyData2D.all_bullet_life_times] entry, else [member BulletVolleyData2D.max_life_time]) times a roll between min and max, seeded like the other rolls by [member bullet_random_seed]. An endless bullet stays endless. 1 and 1 (the default) turn it off; each bullet's time left reads through [method BulletVolley2D.get_bullet_life_time_left].
Outer radius of the random position offset in pixels. See [member bullet_position_jitter_min].

Random position offset per bullet: each bullet moves a random distance between this and [member bullet_position_jitter_max] pixels in a random direction (uniform over the ring's area; an inverted pair swaps). Must be finite and 0 or more. 0 and 0 (default) is off. Randomization applies to shots only: the preview, [method collect_spawn_transforms] and the pattern cache never see it.

Seed of the Randomization rolls. 0 (default) draws from Godot's global random generator, so [method @GlobalScope.seed] reproduces a run. Any other value makes every roll a pure function of the seed, the number of volleys fired, the bullet index and the knob, so the same seed replays the same shots and each knob rolls its own numbers independently of the others.
Upper end of the random extra rotation per bullet. See [member bullet_rotation_min_degrees].

Random extra rotation per bullet, from this angle to [member bullet_rotation_max_degrees] (degrees, any finite values; an inverted pair swaps). The bullet turns around its own position, so its heading changes with it. 0 and 0 (default) is off. Randomization applies to shots only: the preview, [method collect_spawn_transforms] and the pattern cache never see it.
Largest uniform scale factor (mode Uniform). Must be finite and above 0. Equal minimum and maximum give an exact fixed scale.
Largest per-axis scale factors (mode Per Axis). Both components must be finite and above 0.

Smallest uniform scale factor (mode Uniform). Must be finite and above 0. The pair is not checked against each other: if the minimum is above [member bullet_scale_max] the two simply swap roles, so the order you set them in never matters.
Smallest per-axis scale factors (mode Per Axis). Both components must be finite and above 0; each axis swaps with its maximum when inverted.

How each bullet's size is randomized at shot time: Off (default), Uniform (one factor per bullet from [member bullet_scale_min] to [member bullet_scale_max], both axes together) or Per Axis (an independent factor per axis from [member bullet_scale_min_xy] to [member bullet_scale_max_xy]). The factor multiplies the bullet's transform basis, so its collision shape follows; a graze zone that counts bullet size uses the largest scale of the volley. Randomization applies to shots only: the preview, [method collect_spawn_transforms] and the pattern cache never see it.
Upper end of the random speed multiplier. See [member bullet_speed_scale_min].

Random speed multiplier per bullet, from this to [member bullet_speed_scale_max] (an inverted pair swaps). It is applied once when the volley spawns to the bullet's speed, max speed and acceleration, so a faster bullet also accelerates and tops out proportionally; curves and later setters act on the result. Must be finite and 0 or more. 1 and 1 (default) is off. Costs nothing per tick. It has no effect while a speed curve of the spawn data drives the speed (the curve rewrites the speed every tick).
Mirror every other burst volley (fan/spiral chirality flip). The first shot is plain, then shots alternate, for any burst_count.
Shots per burst trigger. Must be between 1 and 1024. Shrinking it during a chain ends the chain at the new count.

Fire multi-volley bursts per trigger: each interval pulls the trigger for burst_count shots spaced burst_interval_sec apart. Mid-burst shots ignore the main interval. Switching it off ends a running chain (with [signal burst_finished]) and its first-shot warning; a plain telegraphed shot keeps its warning.

When above [member burst_interval_sec], every gap between the shots of a burst is drawn between the two (seeded by [member reload_jitter_seed]). 0 (default) keeps it fixed. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Seconds between burst shots. Must be finite and above zero.
The timing of the emitter bullets (see [BulletEmitterData2D]). Empty uses a default timing ([method get_effective_emitter]). Edits reach bullets in flight.

Emitter bullets: every volley fired while this is on fires the pattern of the spawner at [member emitter_spawner_path] from each flying bullet, timed by [member emitter]. The template fires its whole setup and emits its own signals ([signal volley_fired] on the template). Turning it off stops bullets in flight, on resumes them; bullets fired while it was off never emit unless re-armed with [method apply_to_live_volleys] ([constant PatternSpawner2D.LIVE_EMITTER]). Orphaned bullets keep firing through the template (the Clear and Remove [member orphaned_volleys] policies drop their queued shots). A template chain that leads back to this spawner is refused with one error.

The template spawner (a [BulletSpawner2D] or [LaserSpawner2D], normally with its shooting off) whose pattern the bullets fire. Another emitter spawner works too (emitters of emitters); a chain back to this spawner does not. A new template reaches bullets in flight.

The flock rules ([BulletFlock2D]) this spawner's bullets fly by while [member flock_enabled] is on. Example: [code]flock = BulletFlock2D.new()[/code]; raise [member BulletFlock2D.separation_range] for a wider swarm. A new flock, and every edit of this one, reaches bullets already in flight. Empty (the default) flies the default rules: the factory's [method BulletFactory2D.get_default_flock], shared by every empty slot of that factory. Pick a [member BulletFlock2D.preset] to start from Swarm, Fly Together, Keep Distance or Tight Group. Shown while [member flock_enabled] is on.

Master switch of the Flocking group: every volley fired while it is on flies as a flock, where bullets avoid each other, line up and stay grouped. Turning it on is enough (an empty [member flock] flies the default rules); set [member flock] to a new [BulletFlock2D] to tune it (its defaults work for any sprite size; see [BulletFlock2D] for what every setting does and ready-made recipes). For a swarm that holds together, give the bullets a shared goal: turn on [member homing_enabled] (its default [member homing_smoothing] of 5 suits the default flock) or fire a tight pattern. A wide pattern flies apart faster than the flock can hold it, because flocking only turns bullets and never changes their speed. Turning it off stops flocking for the bullets in flight, turning it back on resumes them; bullets fired while it was off never flock ([method flock_live_volleys] arms them). Orphaned volleys keep the last settings. The setup warnings name homing that re-aims every tick ([member homing_smoothing] 0, rotation data or a movement pattern), which leaves the flock only a nudge.

Who flies together: Per Spawner (this spawner's bullets, every shot of it, the default), Shared (every spawner and volley using the same [member flock] resource with Shared: several enemies form one swarm), Per Volley (each shot is its own flock: waves pass through each other). Reaches bullets in flight. Serialized ids: never renumbered.

Node Children source: the node whose [Node2D] children are the graze targets (e.g. an "Enemies" container). Resolved from this spawner; never this spawner or anything under it (a parent inside this spawner finds nothing), a [BulletFactory2D] or anything inside one. After the spawner is freed its volleys keep using the node this path pointed to.
Node Children source: also every [Node2D] below the children (depth-first, tree order), walking through plain [Node]s.

Master switch: every volley this spawner fires is armed with [member graze_zones]. Changes apply to the next shots; volleys already flying keep their zones until [method graze_live_volleys] applies the current settings to them.

Allow-list for every node [member graze_target_source]: only nodes also in this group are graze targets. Empty = everything the source finds. The point sources (Mouse, Global Positions) have no nodes and ignore it.

Global Positions source: every entry is a graze target at that global position (no cap; the editor warns while the list is empty). A list holding a NaN or infinite position is rejected and the old value kept. The points are read every tick: assign a new list (e.g. each frame from a script that tracks players without nodes) and bullets in flight test it on their next tick. A visit belongs to its point's index, so a point that moves keeps its visit; the signals carry a null [code]target[/code] for points.

Node Group source: the group whose [Node2D] members graze this spawner's bullets (e.g. your player's group). Empty by default: name it, or nothing grazes (the editor warns). Members that join later (respawns, enemies spawned after the shot) count from the next scan.

Node Name source: the current scene is scanned for [Node2D]s named like this, compared per [member graze_node_name_match_mode] and [member graze_node_name_case_sensitive] (the same matching as [member homing_node_name]). Never this spawner or its markers, nothing inside a [BulletFactory2D]. A scan walks the scene: with a big scene, give [member graze_update_interval] a few tenths of a second.
Node Name source: compare names with their case (off: "enemy" also matches "Enemy").
Node Name source: how [member graze_node_name] is compared (Exact, Contains, Starts With, Ends With; homing's values).

Also draw this spawner's graze rings while the game runs (debugging aid): edit a zone from a script or the remote inspector and the rings, and every bullet in flight, follow at once. Requires [member graze_show_preview]. This is the only runtime graze preview; every spawner with it on draws its own rings, so turn it on for one spawner to tune a zone that several share.
Line width of the graze preview rings, in pixels. Must be finite and above zero.

Draw every ring of every zone around each resolved target in the zone's [member GrazeZone2D.preview_color]: in the editor, and at runtime only with [member graze_preview_during_runtime]. The rings follow moving targets without rebuilding anything else.

Node Path source: the [Node2D] that grazes this spawner's bullets (a path to another type is rejected). It may be a child of this spawner, never the spawner itself. After the spawner is freed its volleys keep the node this path pointed to.

Who can graze this spawner's bullets: the one place that decides it (a [GrazeZone2D] only says how a graze is measured, so one zone resource works for any target). Node Group (default): the members of [member graze_node_group]. Node Path ([member graze_target_path]), Node Name ([member graze_node_name]) or Node Children ([member graze_children_parent_path]). Mouse (the cursor) and Global Positions ([member graze_global_positions]) are points, not nodes: [signal bullet_grazed] and [signal bullet_graze_exited] carry a null [code]target[/code] for them, and they ignore [member graze_filter_group] and [member graze_update_interval] (read every tick). Every zone rings the same targets. Every source counts all it finds (no cap; past 8 targets each bullet only tests the ones near its motion). The node sources honor [member graze_filter_group] and only keep [Node2D]s inside the tree, not queued for deletion, at a finite position and in the bullets' world, never a [BulletFactory2D] or anything inside one, never this spawner itself; the scans (Node Name, Node Children) never find anything under this spawner either, while Node Group members and Node Path may be its children. The settings are shared with every volley this spawner fired: changing them (or calling [method refresh_graze_targets]) reaches bullets in flight on their next tick, and an open graze visit then moves to the nearest target the bullet is still inside (or ends silently). Orphaned volleys keep the settings after the spawner is freed. Pooled volleys forget them.

Seconds of factory time between target scans; 0 scans every physics tick, so a node that joins (an enemy spawned later) is tested on the next tick. Between scans the targets' positions are still read every tick and a freed or dying target stops counting at once; a newcomer waits for the next scan or [method refresh_graze_targets]. Raise it for costly scans (Node Name over a big scene, many spawners with their own settings); spawners left at the defaults share one scan per group per tick with every factory volley. The point sources (Mouse, Global Positions) are read every tick whatever this says.

Up to 4 [GrazeZone2D] zones armed on every fired volley; null entries are kept and skipped. A shared [code].tres[/code] works across spawners. Assign the whole array: one changed in place still arms its first 4 zones but warns once.
Center the cone on the target. Off starts it to one side.

Blend toward the predicted target position: 0 aims at where the target is now, 1 fully leads it by helper_aimed_prediction_time at its current velocity (needs get_velocity on the target, else aims live).
Seconds of travel to lead the target by at full helper_aimed_prediction.
Aimed cone width in radians.
Spacing between aimed origins so bullets do not stack.
Node the aimed cone points at (also steers the Corridor wall when one is assigned). No target means no bullets in Aimed mode; Corridor falls back to helper_corridor_aim_direction.

Bullet count for helper patterns: every generated pattern draws exactly this many bullets, each on its own spot (Fill Inside, Corridor and Ellipse Wall included). Limited to 1 to [method BulletPatterns2D.get_max_bullets_per_pattern] (default 20000, a project setting): one volley fans out to transforms, instance buffers and physics shapes, so an unlimited value would freeze on a typo. Children, Self and Custom take their count from the markers or the array instead.
Circle bullets face outward (away from the generator); off faces inward (toward it).
Extra facing twist in degrees on top of the circle normal. Must be finite.
Exact circle loop radius in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Fallback aim axis (need not be normalized). The live aimed target wins when one is assigned. Must be finite and non-zero.

Which adjoining side owns a shared corner dot on corner-anchored shapes (Rectangle, Square, Polygon, Triangle, Trapezoid, Diamond, Star): Horizontal Sides (top/bottom own corners, so a top-right dot faces UP), Vertical Sides (left/right own them), Balanced (outgoing edge owns, previous behavior). How corner-anchored polygon loops (Rectangle, Square, Polygon, Triangle, Trapezoid, Diamond, Star) spread leftover slots: Legacy fills the first edges in winding order (equal sides can differ), Symmetric pairs opposite edges so opposite sides stay equal. Interior dots keep at least this many pixels of clearance from corners along their edge (clamped per edge; corners stay pinned). Only shown in Pin Corners mode. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Rotates each closed-loop shape facing: Outline Normal keeps it as generated, +90/-90 Degrees turn it toward the loop tangent. The per-shape facing_offset_deg still applies on top.

The finest grid Fill Inside may shrink to when the bullets do not fit at [member helper_outline_fill_spacing] (for example when [member helper_outline_fill_margin] leaves only a small usable region). The search stops here and places the cells that fit, so a sliver returns fewer bullets than asked, never bullets stacked closer than this, and never a minutes-long search. Lower it if you really want denser fills (cost grows with the square of the shape size over this value; the search never uses a grid finer than 1/1000 of the shape, whatever this says); a [member helper_outline_fill_spacing] you set finer than this is still honored. If the margin leaves no room at all, the pattern pushes the usual "fill inside found no room" error and fires nothing. Must be finite and above zero.

Interior grid cell size in pixels for Fill Inside. Used as-is whenever every bullet fits; when they do not, the spacing shrinks just enough. When more cells fit than bullets, the bullets are picked evenly over the whole shape. Must be finite and above zero.
Shifts every other Fill Inside row by half a cell (honeycomb packing).
How many concentric rings share the volley in Layers placement. 1 is a single exact layer (the default, identical to On Outline). Must be in [1, 64].

How bullets are dealt across layers: Interleaved (bullet i rides layer i % count, winding survives), Sequential (fills contiguous chunks starting from [member helper_outline_layer_start_offset], so small volleys still read as the base shape with offset 0), Outer First (sequential from the outermost ring inward) or Ping Pong (waves 0..last..0, pairs with spin). Layers placement only.

How Layers placement assigns polygon bullets to rings: Shared Loop decimates one loop (outer rings miss corners), Even Per Layer rebuilds an even symmetric loop per ring (corners on every ring). Layers placement only.

Max bullets kept per extra layer (0 = unlimited): overflow is dropped, first-kept in bullet order, so the volley may shrink below helper_bullets_amount. Layer 0 is never capped. Layers placement only.
Fractional growth per layer: each extra ring rescales the shape about the loop center (0.2 = 20% bigger per layer outward). Must be finite in (0, 8]. Layers placement only.
Ring-size progression: Linear steps evenly, Exponential compounds ((1 + step)^L, mirrored reciprocally inward). A non-empty [member helper_outline_layer_scales] overrides both. Layers placement only.

Explicit per-layer scales, entry L % size (e.g. [1.0, 1.5, 1.6] for a tight outer pair). Empty means the formula above. Each entry must be finite in [0.05, 64], at most 64 entries. Layers placement only.
Which side of the base outline extra layers grow toward: Outward (each ring bigger), Inward (rings crowd toward the center), or Both (alternating bigger/smaller). Layers placement only.

Which layer Sequential-family filling starts from (wraps around, so 1 starts on the second ring and the outline fills last). 0 starts on the outline. Only shown — and only consumed — in Layers placement with Sequential or Outer First fill; Interleaved and Ping Pong ignore it. Must be 0 or more.
Slot rotation per successive layered ring (0 = off, negatives wrap): stacked rings interleave angularly instead of sitting in spokes. Layer 0 is never twisted. Layers placement only.

Where closed-loop shape bullets live (Ring, Ellipse, Star, Flower, Rose, Lissajous, Circle, Rectangle, Square, Polygon, Triangle, Trapezoid, Diamond, Heart): On Outline keeps the generated slot loop exactly (single layer, the default), Layers re-spawns the same figure scaled about the loop center (each ring sampled from the true curve), Fill Inside fills the shape's interior with exactly [member helper_bullets_amount] grid cells.
Mirrors the closed-loop slot order (winding flip): bullet 0 moves to the far end of the loop. On-outline and layers layouts only.
Rotates which closed-loop slot becomes bullet 0 (wraps both ways). On-outline and layers layouts only.

Treat the Path2D curve as a loop: the last-to-first stretch is measured so spacing wraps. A curve already drawn as a loop (last point on the first) becomes a clean ring with no doubled seam bullet; two-point outlines always stay open.

Advances the homing queue when a target is reached: per bullet in Per Bullet mode, once for the shared queue in Shared mode.

Parent whose Node2D children are chased for the Node Children source (the whole subtree with [member homing_children_recursive], walking through non-Node2D nodes). Required: an empty or invalid path fires plain volleys and warns once. Nothing under this spawner (and the spawner itself) is ever chased, nor anything inside a [BulletFactory2D].
Includes grandchildren and deeper descendants for the Node Children source.
Seconds of straight flight before volley steering starts (classic aimed-then-homing). 0 steers immediately. Must be finite and 0 or more.
A target counts as reached inside this distance. Predictive, so fast bullets still trigger.
Seconds of steering before volleys fly straight (lets fast players escape). 0 is infinite. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Master switch: every volley chases the configured targets. Off means volleys fly exactly as the spawn data says.
Extra allow-list on top of any source: only targets also in this group are kept. Empty means no filtering.

Fire cone in degrees around the spawner facing including spin (homing only): a volley with resolved targets but none inside half this angle is skipped before spawning (volley_skipped "outside_fire_arc"). A passing volley chases exactly the targets the cone approved (one resolution per shot). Empty resolutions still fire plain volleys; the mouse source never resolves, so the cone ignores it. 0 is omnidirectional. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Position chased per volley for the Global Position source. Must be finite.
Volley steering pauses while the bullet is farther than this from its target. 0 is unlimited. Must be finite and 0 or more.

Detection radius around the effective generator (the volley's muzzle: [member transforms_generator_path] when set, else the spawner) for the node group, node name, and node children sources (never Node Path, which names one node). Nearest selection measures from the same point. 0 is unlimited.

How many targets enter the queue. 1 is classic single-target homing. Only the node group, node name, and node children sources use it. Must be 1 or more; there is no upper cap (homing queues hold as many targets as you give them).
0 shares one target queue across the whole volley, 1 gives every bullet its own queue (same targets each).

Polled group for the Node Group source (empty by default: name it, or volleys fly without homing and the editor warns). Only Node2D members can be chased; other members, the spawner itself, nodes queued for deletion and anything the shared filter refuses (see [member homing_target_source]) are skipped. The spawner's own children may be members.

Name pattern chased for the Node Name source (empty by default: name it). The whole scene is scanned, so dynamically spawned enemies are found with no group setup. The spawner itself and its child markers never match, and [BulletFactory2D] subtrees (volleys, attachments, effects) are never scanned. Prefer the Node Group source in large scenes: the scan visits every node once per volley.
Compares node names strictly. Off (default) matches "Player" against "PlAyEr".
How the node name source compares names: exact, contains, starts with, or ends with.
Fans smoothing out per bullet: bullet i steers with start + step times i.

Seed for homing random-target selection ([constant BulletSpawner2D.HOMING_SELECT_RANDOM]) only. 0 is non-deterministic, otherwise picks reproduce. Only shown when that selection is active. Does not affect steering, smoothing, retargeting or any bullet pattern.

When on, the homing reach test adds the bullet's own size: [code]homing_distance_before_reached[/code] is measured from the bullet's EDGE (its collision shape's bounding radius times its own scale) instead of its center, so a big or randomly scaled bullet reaches (and auto-pops, and fires the reached signal) when it visibly touches its target. Off (the default) keeps the center-to-center distance. Pair it with the Randomization group's [member bullet_scale_mode]: every bullet counts its own size. Example: a 64 px boulder with [code]homing_distance_before_reached = 5[/code] reaches when its edge is 5 px from the target.
Seconds between automatic retarget passes. Must be above zero.
0 leaves flying volleys alone, On Interval re-resolves and replaces their queues every interval. On by default so group, name, and children tracking stays live as members spawn and die.

Explicit time to the first retarget pass. 0 (default) staggers it per spawner automatically, so many spawners never scene-scan on the same tick. The period stays homing_retarget_interval_sec. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Retargeting re-aims every tracked live volley. Turn off to re-aim only the newest volley, letting older ones fly at whatever they chased last.

Max turn rate in radians per second. 0 snaps instantly. A bullet cannot turn tighter than speed / smoothing pixels, so to be sure it hits, keep that radius smaller than the target's hitbox (raise the smoothing for fast bullets or small targets).
Per-bullet smoothing of the first bullet.
Per-bullet smoothing growth per bullet. May be negative, results clamp at 0.
Lets homing steer the bullet facing. Turn off only when a movement pattern, rotation data, or orbiting texture mode already owns the facing, otherwise homing steers nothing.

Node chased per volley for the Node Path source. Must point at a live Node2D in the tree: a freed, removed or dying target (or one the shared filter refuses, see [member homing_target_source]) means the volley flies without homing (warned once). It may be this spawner itself ([code].[/code]: bullets fly back to it) or one of its children. Inside the tree, a path to a non-Node2D is rejected and the old value kept; an unresolved path is accepted (the node may be added later).
Which detected nodes become targets: nearest to the spawner, random, tree order, round robin across volleys, or dealt across bullets (Per Bullet mode only).

Where volley targets come from: a node group, the mouse cursor, a global position snapshot, a node path, a node name, or a node's children. Each source shows its own settings, like the pattern_source helper patterns do. The node sources share one filter with graze: only [Node2D]s inside the tree, not queued for deletion, at a finite position and in the bullets' world, never a [BulletFactory2D] or anything inside one. The scans (Node Name, Node Children) never find this spawner or anything under it; Node Group members may be its children but never the spawner itself; Node Path may name the spawner itself (bullets fly back to it, or orbit it with [member orbiting_enabled]) or its children. When a shot finds no target it still fires as a plain volley, and a warning explaining why prints once per homing configuration (changing any homing target setting re-arms it).
Seconds between target position refreshes. 0 refreshes every tick.

Bullets fired while the spawner moves inherit its movement velocity ([method get_movement_velocity] x [member movement_velocity_inherit_factor]), so a moving turret's shots carry its momentum for their whole life. Homing bullets aim through that momentum (they cancel it across the line of sight), but only while their own speed is larger than the sideways part of the inherited velocity: lower the factor for slow homing bullets. Off by default.

Soft live-bullet fuse: 0 is unlimited, otherwise a shot is skipped (volley_skipped "over_budget") while this spawner's live bullets (homing and plain volleys, counted via the factory) reach this count. The check runs before any pattern work, so a stalled spawner costs nothing. Retargeting is not affected. The census is O(factory volleys) per trigger pull: fine for a handful of budgeted spawners.

The most shots one timer (auto-fire, a burst chain, a pattern list) fires in one frame. An interval shorter than a frame, or a late frame, repays up to this many shots; then the timer resyncs and drops the rest of its backlog. [code]1[/code] never repays a hitch: an overloaded game degrades by firing less instead of piling more volleys onto slow frames. Must be >= 1.

Auto-shooting stops after this many volleys. -1 is infinite, 0 disables auto-shooting ([method shoot_once] still works). Lowering the cap below the fired count emits [signal shooting_stopped] (raising it back emits [signal shooting_started]); [signal shooting_finished] fires once from the volley that trips the cap, so a volley_fired handler that lowers the cap never double-fires it. Untouched by [method fire_n_volleys].

Start moving automatically on ready, and when [member movement_enabled] is switched on at runtime (switched on while the spawner is out of the tree, it starts when the spawner enters it again). Off: call [method movement_play] yourself.
Sample the path with cubic interpolation (the [code]cubic[/code] argument of [method Curve2D.sample_baked]) for smoother motion on coarse bakes. Off: linear between baked points (cheaper).
Direction of the first leg: Forward (path start to end) or Reverse (end to start).
Seconds per leg when [member movement_timing] is Duration. Must be finite and greater than 0.
[enum Tween.EaseType] applied to each leg's progress (In, Out, In Out, Out In), exactly like a Tween. Hidden when [member movement_progress_curve] is set.

Master switch: the spawner node travels along [member movement_path] at runtime (never in the editor). Movement runs before shooting and the preview each frame, so shots and the gizmo use the updated pose. Every pattern keeps working while moving; patterns that follow the spawner stay baked (no regeneration per shot).
Dwell time at each endpoint between legs (Loop and Ping Pong). Not applied after the final leg.
Once: one leg, then [signal movement_finished]. Loop: every leg starts again from the path start (a jump back, no sweep). Ping Pong: the direction alternates each leg.
How many legs Loop and Ping Pong run (0 = forever). Ping Pong counts each direction, so 2 = there and back. Ignored in Once mode.
The [Path2D] to follow. It must be in the tree with a non-empty curve; otherwise the spawner stays where it is and a warning prints once.

Optional [Curve] mapping leg time (x, 0..1) to path progress (y). Overrides [member movement_transition] and [member movement_ease]. Progress outside 0..1 is clamped to the path ends; non-finite samples fall back to linear.
Rotate the spawner to face its direction of travel (it turns around on reverse legs).
Extra rotation in degrees on top of the path-facing rotation (for example 90 when the art points up).
Attach: the spawner sits on the path itself (like [PathFollow2D]). Relative To Start: the path's shape is replayed from where the spawner starts, so a path drawn anywhere works as a motion template.
Pixels per second when [member movement_timing] is Speed (each leg takes path length / speed). Must be finite and greater than 0.
Seconds to wait at the start pose before the first leg moves; applied on every fresh start.
Fraction (0..1) of the first leg already elapsed when a run starts.
Duration: each leg takes [member movement_duration_sec]. Speed: each leg takes path length / [member movement_speed].
[enum Tween.TransitionType] easing each leg (Linear, Sine, Quint, Back, ...), identical to a Tween. Hidden when [member movement_progress_curve] is set.
Multiplier on the inherited movement velocity (1 = full momentum, 0.5 = half, negative = backwards).

Orbit direction. DontMove means escort: bullets hold a fixed slot on the ring and follow the target without circling. OrbitRandom rolls OrbitLeft or OrbitRight per bullet when the volley spawns (never DontMove); live volleys keep their rolled direction on retarget passes, so switching to OrbitRandom mid-flight only affects new volleys.

Bullets ring their homing target once they arrive. Needs [member homing_enabled]: orbiting without homing does nothing (volleys fly straight; one warning per configuration, and the setup warnings list it). A freed mid-flight target never crashes: dead entries trim out of the queue, non-finite frames hold the bullet still for one tick, and the lock follows [member orbiting_lock_policy].

Deadzone radius in pixels, used only when [member orbiting_follow_mode] is FollowDeadzone. The ring center stays pinned while the target moves within this distance of the lock point, then re-pins to the target.

How the locked ring follows a moving target. FollowTarget tracks the target 1:1. FollowDeadzone pins the ring center until the target walks farther than [member orbiting_follow_deadzone] from it, absorbing jitter. Anchored freezes the ring where it locked and ignores target motion entirely.

What drops the orbit lock. RelockAlways re-acquires the radius on every retarget. StayLocked never unlocks on retarget or empty queues: once locked, bullets keep their angle and center until you explicitly disable orbiting, clear targets, or the target is freed. RelockOnTargetChange unlocks only when the front target is a different target than the one the bullet locked onto, so the same moving Node2D never breaks the ring. A freed target trims out of the queue instead of crashing: RelockAlways and RelockOnTargetChange fly toward the next live target, StayLocked rides out the gap and re-pins silently when a target returns. For a bodyguard ring on a moving Node2D use StayLocked with FollowTarget (or FollowDeadzone) and a stationary retarget mode.
Orbit ring radius in pixels. Must be at least 0.01.
Fans the radius out per bullet: bullet i orbits with start + step times i (concentric shells).
Orbit radius of the first bullet in linear mode.
Orbit radius growth per bullet in linear mode. May be negative, results clamp at 0.01.

When on, locked OrbitLeft/OrbitRight bullets translate 1:1 with the target and keep circling, exactly like DontMove escorts. When off, locked bullets chase the ring clamped to speed times delta and trail behind fast targets.
How bullet textures face while physically orbiting.

What happens to this spawner's live volleys when the spawner is freed (an enemy dying with its turret, a scene change), in every factory it fired into (also one it used before [method PatternSpawner2D.set_bullet_factory] switched it). Reparenting never triggers it. Freed from user code inside a factory operation (an attachment callback of a clear), Clear and Remove apply right after that operation. - [constant ORPHANED_VOLLEYS_KEEP_FLYING] (default): the bullets fly on, but their hits reach nobody: signal connections live on the emitter, so every connection on the freed spawner is gone, even ones whose callback is on a long-lived node. The first unhandled hit prints one warning explaining this. - [constant ORPHANED_VOLLEYS_HAND_TO_FACTORY]: the volleys become factory-owned, so [signal BulletFactory2D.area_entered] and the other factory signals report their hits. The only way an orphan's hits can still be handled. - [constant ORPHANED_VOLLEYS_CLEAR]: every live bullet is cleared with its On Clear effects (a wave that vanishes with its source). - [constant ORPHANED_VOLLEYS_REMOVE]: every live bullet disappears silently and its volley returns to the pool. To keep hit handlers working while the spawner lives, connect to the spawner's signals from a node that outlives it, or set [member BulletVolleyData2D.emit_collision_signals] to [code]false[/code] for bullets that intentionally report nothing.

Auto (default): pattern transforms are generated once and re-posed per shot whenever the pattern provably follows the generator (rigidly, or by translation only); any pattern-affecting property change rebakes automatically. Sources that read outside state (From Children, Aimed, Corridor, Custom, Path2D) and unseeded random patterns always regenerate. A moving or spinning spawner never needs Off. Off: regenerate every shot, for debugging or for scripts that change pattern inputs behind the setters' back.

Scales the whole pattern around the generator (positions and bullet size grow together). 1.0 keeps it as is, 0 collapses it onto the generator, negatives mirror it. Compose with transforms_scale for big-layout + big-bullet looks.

Where volley transforms come from: children markers (0), this generator itself (1), or one of 31 procedural helper patterns (2-32: Grid, Ring, Fan, Spiral, Line, Aimed, Flower, Ellipse, Rain, Scatter, Star Polygon, Multi Spiral, Cross, Star, Heart, Wave, Waterfall, Lattice, Rose, Counter Spiral, Corridor, Lissajous, Custom, Circle, Rectangle, Square, Polygon, Path2D, Triangle, Trapezoid, Diamond). Only the active pattern's options show in the inspector. Every helper draws exactly [member helper_bullets_amount] bullets at distinct spots. Pipeline per volley: generate (with outline placement, fill or layers for the loop shapes), then spin, then pattern/local scale, then helper_skip_indices (so skip indexes match the preview).
Preview arrow color.
Gap in pixels between dot edge and arrow tail.
Preview arrow head length in pixels.
Preview arrow head width in pixels.
Preview arrow length in pixels (multiplied by pattern_scale and transforms_scale, so glyphs stay proportional to the layout).
Preview arrow shaft width in pixels.
Collision-ring overlay color.
Collision-ring overlay line width in pixels.
Preview dot color.
Preview dot radius in pixels (multiplied by pattern_scale and transforms_scale, so glyphs stay proportional to the layout).

When true and spawn_data carries a valid collision shape, the dots layer also draws one outline circle per dot with the shape's bounding radius (circle r, rect min/2, capsule height/2). Compare hitbox vs visual directly in the editor.
Emphasis color for bullet 0 in the preview (pattern start: anchor, reverse, loop seam). Drawn bigger on top of the regular dot.

Extra outline-layer ring color (Layers placement only): one yellow closed ring per ring beyond the base outline, drawn under the dots with the same width as the base track and never antialiased. Same alpha as the base track by default. Empty unless layers are active (count above 1 with valid spacing).

Track underlay color: the shape/loop/curve bullets ride on, drawn as segments under the dots so sparse volleys still show the whole track. Distinct from dots, arrows and the first-bullet marker by default.
Track underlay line width in pixels (multiplied by nothing: absolute screen-ish size). 0 hides the track. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Whether [member preview_z_index] is relative to this spawner's own z order (default) or absolute.

The z index of the pattern preview (dots, arrows and laser beam bands) and of the runtime graze ring preview (default 4000: over most of the game). Lower it when a background or a UI layer must stay on top. Edits reach the live preview at once. Between -4096 and 4096.

Which callback runs the spawner at runtime: movement, spin, countdowns and shots. [constant PROCESS_IDLE] (the default) runs every rendered frame. [constant PROCESS_PHYSICS] runs every physics tick: shots line up with the bullets' own ticks, so a stream's bullets sit exactly [code]speed x interval[/code] apart at any frame rate (with Idle, a shot between two ticks still moves a full step on the next one). Pair Physics with Godot's physics interpolation for smooth spawner motion. The editor preview always refreshes per frame.

Reload jitter in seconds: each auto volley waits shoot_interval_sec +/- uniform jitter (seeded by [member reload_jitter_seed], floored at 0.001s so fast intervals keep working with jitter on). 0 is exact. Must be finite and 0 or more.

Seed for every timing roll: [member reload_jitter_sec] and the ranges of [member shoot_interval_max_sec], [member burst_interval_max_sec] and [member telegraph_max_sec]. 0 is non-deterministic, otherwise the timing sequence reproduces exactly; different seeds give independent sequences. Does not affect any bullet pattern or homing pick.
Delay before the first automatic volley. Applied when the spawner becomes ready and by [method reset_shooting]. Must be finite and 0 or more.

When above [member shoot_interval_sec], every wait between shots is drawn between the two (seeded by [member reload_jitter_seed] like the reload jitter, which then adds its own spread on top). 0 (default) keeps the interval fixed. Must be finite and 0 or more.

Seconds between automatic volleys. Must be above zero. Shortening it also shortens the wait already running, down to the longest wait the settings can still roll ([member shoot_interval_max_sec], [member reload_jitter_sec]): setting the same value never cuts a rolled wait, and the initial delay ([member shoot_initial_delay_sec]) is never cut. Runs on an accumulator: overshoot carries over so the average rate is exact at any value (fast intervals repay every due volley in the same tick, up to [member max_shots_per_frame] per frame; backlogs beyond that resync instead of bursting). With bursts or a telegraph the interval starts after the chain: a trigger pull waits the interval, then the whole chain (telegraph, burst shots) plays before the next wait begins. Burst steps and pattern-list entries keep their own average rate the same way.

When the factory's [member BulletFactory2D.despawn_bounds_enabled] is on, a spawner whose muzzle (its global position plus the spawn position offset) is outside [member BulletFactory2D.despawn_bounds_rect] does not shoot: the bullets would be culled on their first tick. The shot is reported through [signal volley_skipped] with the reason "outside_despawn_bounds" (no error), auto-fire keeps its rhythm, and the spawner shoots again as soon as the muzzle is inside. Edges count as inside. Turn this on to shoot from outside anyway (bullets that fly inwards survive the cull).
Master switch for automatic shooting. [method shoot_once] works regardless.
Shows one dot and facing arrow per bullet in the editor. Follows the generator live. Never saved to the scene.

Also shows the preview while the game runs. Off by default. Switched off at runtime, the preview goes down at once; a spawner that leaves the tree takes its preview off an external [member transforms_generator] too (rebuilt when it enters again).

Stacked [BulletSoundData2D] entries (nulls allowed, skipped; a [LaserSoundData2D] is refused with one error, keeping the old value). Each entry plays one of its [member BulletSoundData2D.streams] when its trigger fires, subject to its own limits. On Shot and On Telegraph entries offer from the spawner itself; the rest fire from the volley.

Master switch: every volley this spawner fires is armed with [member sound_effects]. Changes apply to the next shots; volleys already flying keep their entries until [method sound_live_volleys] applies the current settings to them.
Node Children source: Node2D children of this parent.
Node Children source: scan the whole subtree, not just direct children.
Allow-list for every node source: only nodes in this group count (empty counts everything found).
Global Positions source: one listener per entry (finite only), read every sweep. Points never follow.

Node Group source: Node2D members of this group (empty by default: the developer names it). Player-ears example: a fixed camera shows the whole arena while the ears follow the player, so set the source to Node Group and the group to [code]"player"[/code]: near misses on the player sound loud wherever the camera sits. An empty result falls back to Godot's listener and warns once, naming the empty setting.
Node Name source: Node2Ds named like this (scene scan, never inside a factory or this spawner).
Node Name source: match case-sensitively.
How sound_listener_node_name matches (homing's values): Exact, Contains, Starts With, Ends With.
Node Path source: the Node2D at this path.

Who the sounds are measured from: Godot's own 2D listener, or listeners picked like graze/homing targets. Shared with every volley this spawner fired, so edits reach bullets in flight; orphaned volleys keep the settings. Each offer and each sweep measures from the nearest listener to the event (tree order breaks ties); a source that finds nobody falls back to Godot's listener. Example: source Node Group with [member sound_listener_node_group] set to the player group makes enemy shots louder as they approach the player, whatever the camera does.
Seconds between listener scans (factory time); 0 scans every physics tick. Positions stay live between scans.

Mix trim added to every entry's volume on top of its own volume_db (plus each play's random rolls), before the entry's [member BulletSoundData2D.volume_min_db]..[member BulletSoundData2D.volume_max_db] clamp. Between -80 and 24.

Bullet data for each volley. A shot only reads it (the pattern's transforms travel separately), so sharing one resource between spawners is safe. With a split chain armed the spawner keeps a copy for the children of its bullets (an edit made after a shot never reaches bullets already flying); the copy is refreshed after the resource changes or is replaced. A setter writing the value a property already holds is not a change. Per-shot values (who fired, a damage snapshot) belong on the fired volley, for example [member BulletVolley2D.shared_bullets_custom_data] from a [signal volley_fired] handler, not on this resource: every real edit costs the next shot a refresh.

Flat global offset added to every bullet right after spawn (muzzle offsets, spawn-then-nudge). Zero disables the pass. Applied through the engine teleport path, so shapes, attachments, and interpolation stay in sync. Must be finite.

How [member spawn_position_offset] applies. Global (default, the historical behaviour): a world-space shift for every volley. Local: a muzzle offset in the generator's frame, so it turns and scales with the spawner. The preview draws the offset where bullets actually spawn, in both spaces.
How far the pattern swings each way in oscillate mode.
Rotates each volley around the generator at runtime. Editor preview stays still.
Swings per second in oscillate mode.
0 rotates forever, 1 swings back and forth (see amplitude and frequency).

When on, the spin starts at a random phase instead of 0: a random angle for a continuous spin, a random point of the period for an oscillating one. Rolled when the spawner enters play and on every [method reset_spin_angle], seeded by [member bullet_random_seed]. Keeps many spawners from spinning in lockstep.
Spin speed in continuous mode. Positive is clockwise.

The split chain fired volleys carry: [member BulletSplitData2D.stages][code][d][/code] decides how generation [code]d[/code] splits. Edits reach bullets already in flight. Children copy this spawner's spawn data (or the stage's [member BulletSplitStage2D.child_data]) and stay owned by this spawner.

Turns splitting on for volleys fired from now on. Turning it off stops splitting for bullets already in flight (on again resumes them); bullets fired while it was off never split. Orphaned volleys keep the last settings.

Warn before firing: emits volley_telegraphed with the current aim, then fires after telegraph_sec (or a random time up to [member telegraph_max_sec]; with both at 0 nothing warns). Transforms re-collect at fire time. The aim snapshot runs the aimed target's [code]get_velocity[/code]: a script there that resets the wave, ends the burst or turns telegraphs off cancels the warning it interrupted. A burst whose first-shot warning cannot start (the muzzle outside the despawn bounds) retries a burst interval later, warning first again.
When above [member telegraph_sec], every warning lasts a random time between the two (seeded by [member reload_jitter_seed]). 0 (default) keeps it fixed. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Warning time before the volley fires. Must be finite and 0 or more.

The spawner's own clock speed. Its shot interval, initial delay, burst and telegraph timers, pattern list, retarget interval, spin and Path2D movement all run on real delta times this value times [member BulletFactory2D.time_scale] of the factory it serves: 1 is real time, 0.5 slow motion, 0 freezes the spawner and it resumes with exactly the time it had left. While it lives, the bullets it fired follow the same product unless [member time_scale_affects_volleys] is off. Must be finite and 0 or more. A very large value cannot spiral: at most 8 shots per frame fire and the rest of the backlog is dropped.

When on (default), the volleys this spawner fired run at its [member time_scale] too (motion, lifetime, timers), as long as the spawner exists; after it is freed they follow the factory scale only. Turn it off to slow just the spawner's own actions while its bullets keep flying at the factory scale. [member inherit_movement_velocity] reports the path speed in the spawner's own time.

Node patterns are built on. Empty means this spawner. Point it at another Node2D to move children markers, helper shapes, spin pivot, scale center, and the preview there. Inside the tree, a path to a non-Node2D is rejected (old value kept).

Per-bullet size scale: multiplies each spawn transform's local basis (texture size) without moving its position. 1.0 keeps sizes as generated, 0 hides bullets in place, negatives mirror them. Must be finite.

A time scale for everything this spawner fired, never for the spawner itself: [code]0.0[/code] freezes its bullets in place (the classic time stop) while it keeps moving and firing, [code]0.5[/code] halves their speed, animations, timers and lifetimes. Multiplies the factory's [member BulletFactory2D.time_scale] and, while [member time_scale_affects_volleys] is on, [member time_scale]. Orphans (the spawner freed) leave it. Must be finite and [code]>= 0[/code].

signal.name: area_entered
signal.description: Fired live when one of this spawner's bullets enters an area; same contract as [signal BulletFactory2D.area_entered] (the factory stays silent for spawner volleys). Connections live on the spawner: if it is freed they are gone, see [member orphaned_volleys].

signal.name: body_entered
signal.description: Fired live when one of this spawner's bullets hits a body; same contract as [signal BulletFactory2D.body_entered].

signal.name: bounce_area_entered
signal.description: Fired when one of this spawner's bullets bounces off an area. A consumed bounce fires both this and [signal area_entered].

signal.name: bounce_body_entered
signal.description: Fired when one of this spawner's bullets bounces off a body. A consumed bounce fires both this and [signal body_entered].

signal.name: bullet_graze_exited
signal.description: Fired when one of this spawner's bullets leaves a graze zone alive after grazing it. [param target] is null for the point sources. Same payload and contract as [signal BulletFactory2D.bullet_graze_exited], which fires right after this one.

signal.name: bullet_grazed
signal.description: Fired live when one of this spawner's bullets grazes a ring of a zone (see [GrazeZone2D]). [param target] is null for the point sources (Mouse, Global Positions). Same payload and contract as [signal BulletFactory2D.bullet_grazed], which fires right after this one for the same graze: count graze on one of the two. Once this spawner is freed its flying bullets keep grazing and only the factory signal fires.

signal.name: bullet_split
signal.description: A bullet of this spawner split: [param children] is the new volley (owned by this spawner, already armed), spawned at [param position] where the parent died. [param cause] is one of the [code]BulletVolley2D.SPLIT_CAUSE_*[/code] constants and [param depth] the children's generation. Emitted once per parent after the factory sweep in which it died. An orphaned volley's splits are silent (like its hits) unless [member orphaned_volleys] handed it to the factory.

signal.name: homing_targets_resolved
signal.description: Fired once per homing volley with the resolved targets (Node2D or Vector2 entries), before [signal volley_homing_configured]. Empty for the Mouse source and for volleys that found nothing. Not fired while homing is off. A handler may queue_free the volley: the shot is then dropped (volley_skipped "dropped").

signal.name: life_time_over
signal.description: Fired live when this spawner's bullets expire (needs the lifetime signal enabled in the spawn data); same contract as [signal BulletFactory2D.life_time_over]: the listed bullets are alive in the handler and die right after it unless their life was extended.

signal.name: pre_shoot
signal.description: Last-chance hook fired after the volley has spawned, been stamped and armed with this spawner's graze, sound, flocking and splitting settings, but before the muzzle offset, homing and orbiting are configured and before volley_fired. What a handler arms instead (graze_set_zones, sound_set_effects, flock_join, split_set_data) is kept. Handlers may tweak the live volley through its API (speed ramp, difficulty scale); the spawn data has already been consumed at this point. Same handler contract as volley_fired: never call shoot_once from here (use shoot_once_deferred).

signal.name: retarget_applied
signal.description: Fired after an automatic interval retarget pass that touched at least one volley. HUD and wave logic can observe tracking health from this.

signal.name: volley_bullet_homing_target_reached
signal.description: Fired live when a bullet of one of this spawner's volleys reaches its homing target (also emitted on the volley as [signal BulletVolley2D.bullet_homing_target_reached]). Target is null for position and mouse targets. Connect here rather than on volley instances: a volley drops its own connections when it returns to the pool.

signal.name: volley_fired
signal.description: Fired for every volley, with a 1-based counter.

signal.name: volley_homing_configured
signal.description: Fired for every homing/orbiting volley right after it is configured: in a shot before [signal volley_fired] ([param volley_index] = that shot's number), and when homing configures a volley outside a shot (split children, [method apply_to_live_volleys], a parked volley's wake), where [param volley_index] is the number the next shot will get. Only fires when homing or orbiting is enabled.

constants.constant: No spawner colors: the volleys draw the spawn data's own colors, or none.

Bullet [code]i[/code] of [code]n[/code] samples the gradient at [code]i / (n - 1)[/code] (from its start to its end across the pattern): a rainbow ring in one setting. [member bullet_color_shift_per_shot] scrolls it.
Every bullet samples a random point of the gradient, seeded by [member bullet_random_seed] (0 uses Godot's global random generator).
The whole shot wears one color, stepping along the gradient every shot (see [member bullet_color_cycle_shots]).
One homing queue shared by every bullet of the volley.
Every bullet owns its own homing queue (same targets each).
Targets are polled from [member homing_node_group].
Targets chase the mouse cursor position.
Targets chase the [member homing_global_position] snapshot.
Targets chase the Node2D at [member homing_target_path].
Targets are scanned by node name ([member homing_node_name]).
Targets are the Node2D children of [member homing_children_parent_path].
Picks the closest nodes to the spawner, up to [member homing_max_targets].
Picks random nodes, up to [member homing_max_targets].
Picks nodes in tree order, up to [member homing_max_targets].
Cycles through the group across volleys, up to [member homing_max_targets] each.
Deals targets across bullets in Per Bullet mode (bullet i chases pool[i % pool]). Ignored in Shared mode.
Flying volleys keep the targets they spawned with.
Flying volleys are re-aimed every [member homing_retarget_interval_sec].
Freed spawner: its bullets keep flying; their hits reach nobody (one warning explains why).
Freed spawner: its volleys become factory-owned and report on the [BulletFactory2D] signals.
Freed spawner: its live bullets are cleared with their On Clear effects.
Freed spawner: its live bullets disappear silently and the volleys return to the pool.
